 Kaitlyn McCormick USA TODAY Nov. 18, 2026, 11:23 a.m. ET Hear this story Experts have warned that without Congressional interference, some Social Security payment funding could run dry by 2032 .
 Does this impact your disability payments?
 Here's what the latest Social Security Administration reports say.
 If Social Security shrinks, will my disability payment end?
 While the latest SSA Trustee Reports predict funding for retirement benefits to end in 2032, disability benefits are another story.

The Disability Insurance Trust Fund is a different funding source than Social Security's Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund. The DI is anticipated to pay 100% of its scheduled benefits through 2100, its long-range forecast window.
 Are Social Security OASI and DI the same?
 No. The OASI and DI Trust Funds are two different funds that finance different parts of the Social Security program.
 The OASIA Trust Fund funds retirement and survivor benefits, while the DI Trust Fund funds Social Security Disability payments.
 How is Social Security funded? Where does Social Security come from
 Per the Trustee Report, OASI and DI funding come primarily from taxes and interest.
 This includes payroll taxes contributed by employees, employers and self-employed individuals.
 Kaitlyn McCormick is a Philadelphia-based reporter writing all things cost of living related for USA TODAY .
